stories.title: Sunday tea with June
stories.story: Every Sunday afternoon, Rose and her little sister June had tea at the kitchen table in the Hartley house, using their mother Edith's blue-rimmed cups. Rose was eight and poured very carefully. They kept the tradition for over sixty years, later by phone.
hints: You and your sister had a Sunday ritual...
Something warm, in your mother's blue cups...
stories.quilt_square: a teapot and two small teacups with blue rims on a checked tablecloth

stories.title: First date at the Lyric
stories.story: Rose and Frank's first date was a Saturday matinee at the Lyric Theatre in Duluth. Frank was so nervous he bought two bags of popcorn and dropped one. Rose kept the ticket stub in her jewellery box.
hints: A Saturday afternoon in Duluth, with Frank...
Popcorn, and a little cinema on First Street...
stories.quilt_square: an old cinema ticket and a striped popcorn bag

stories.title: The silver rose brooch
stories.story: On their wedding day in June 1969, Frank's mother Margaret pinned a small silver rose brooch to Rose's dress and said Rose should always wear a rose. Rose wore it to every family wedding after that.
hints: A gift on your wedding day...
Something small, silver, shaped like a rose...
stories.quilt_square: a small silver rose brooch on a ribbon

stories.title: Summers at Loon Lake
stories.story: From 1972, the Ellis family spent every summer at a small cabin on Loon Lake with a green door and a wooden dock. Frank fished at dawn and caught almost nothing. Rose taught Anne to swim off the dock, and they picked wild blueberries along the shore.
hints: The place by the water, every summer...
A cabin with a green door, and a dock...
stories.quilt_square: a small cabin with a green door beside a lake and a wooden dock

stories.title: Bluebell, the blue car
stories.story: Frank rebuilt an old powder-blue station wagon in their garage over one winter and Rose named it Bluebell. It took the whole family to Loon Lake every summer, with Michael singing in the back seat. Rose kept Bluebell's key long after the car was gone.
hints: Frank built something in the garage one winter...
It was blue, and you gave it a flower's name...
stories.quilt_square: a powder-blue station wagon on a country road

stories.title: Blueberry buckle for every birthday
stories.story: Rose baked her blueberry buckle for every family birthday in the yellow Ely kitchen, using berries saved from Loon Lake. She wrote the recipe on a card for Anne in 1983, with a note at the bottom: more berries than you think.
hints: Something you baked for every birthday...
It had berries from the lake in it...
stories.quilt_square: a blueberry cake on a plate with a few loose blueberries

Key: Rose hesitates, gets one hint, still unsure, says 'blue... Frank's car'. Magpie gently tells the Bluebell story, then plays Priya's voice clip: 'Here's Priya talking about Bluebell.' She smiles. Fragment saved for review.
Recipe card: short and happy, then Magpie ends the session warmly.
Optional beat: show the 'Talk about something else' button once, briefly, to prove she is never stuck.

agent_rules: Use only confirmed Engram facts. Never invent a name, place, date or event.
Never quiz, test or correct Rose. If she says something different, accept it warmly and save it for family review.
Never mention illness, memory, death, or that she has forgotten something.
Ask open, warm questions first. Hint gently twice at most. Then tell the story as a gift.
End gently if she seems tired or upset.
